Your ads worked. People are adding to cart. But the orders don&#x27;t match the clicks. Picture your shopper. They&#x27;re on the sofa with one thumb free, ready to buy. Then checkout asks them to type a card number and make an account. That&#x27;s often where the sale slips away. The shopper already decided to buy, so there&#x27;s nothing left to persuade. Adobe&#x27;s 2026 forecast puts mobile at 57.4% of online holiday spend. Pay later is forecast at $21.3 billion, and 82% of it comes through mobile. Your busiest days get decided on a small screen. Here are 5 things that make paying on a phone easier: 1️⃣ One-tap payment buttons at the top Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal let people pay without typing a card number or address. Without them, your shopper types on glass and gives up. With them, paying takes seconds, not minutes. 2️⃣ Pay later shown near the price Some shoppers see the price and quietly decide it&#x27;s too much. A pay in four message beside it changes that moment. They see the real amount per payment and keep going. 3️⃣ Fewer form fields Every box is a small tax on patience, and typing on a phone is slow. Do you really need a company name to ship a parcel? Remove what you don&#x27;t need and the form feels shorter. 4️⃣ Checkout without making an account Being asked to sign up right when they&#x27;re ready to pay feels like a wall. Many shoppers just close the tab. Let them pay first and offer an account afterward. 5️⃣ A real test order on a real phone Buy something from your own store on your own phone. Notice every spot where you hesitate. Your customers hesitate in the same places, and you&#x27;ll see it before they do. Most of these are small changes, not a rebuild. You can fix several this week. When did you last buy from your own store on your phone?
